summary: Monolith: ASP.NET Core + Azure SQL Database serving Blazor (ASP.NET Core), hosted on Azure App Service (Central India, Pune). Estimated $50-290/month (within the $300 budget).

architecture_rationale.text: A single deployable is the fastest and cheapest option for a 2-person team building a internal_tool with 1,500 users. Over-engineering guard: microservices rejected: 2 engineer(s), no DevOps cannot absorb the operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Web - Blazor (ASP.NET Core): Chosen because team already works in csharp (team.languages); strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=5; strong time-to-market (4/5) with priorities.time_to_market=5; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=4.

alternatives.why_not: Blazor scores higher on maintainability and reuse of existing systems (fit 8.7 vs 9.4).
Blazor scores higher on maintainability and reuse of existing systems (fit 8.4 vs 9.4).

tradeoffs: Interactive Server mode keeps a SignalR circuit per user
WebAssembly mode has a larger first download

backend.justification: Chosen because team already works in csharp (team.languages); strong maintainability (5/5) with priorities.maintainability=5; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=4; Microsoft.Identity.Web makes Entra ID SSO a configuration task.

alternatives.why_not: Sync batches and large uploads run into function time/size limits. ASP.NET Core scores higher on maintainability and reuse of existing systems (fit 9.1 vs 11.0).

Excluded by hard constraint: cloud_preference=azure: Firebase (Firestore + Auth + Functions) is a Google Cloud service.

database.justification: Chosen because reuses the existing 'On-prem SQL Server 2019'; relational integrity and transactions for a internal_tool domain; strong security (5/5) with priorities.security=4; strong maintainability (4/5) with priorities.maintainability=5. Managed as Azure SQL Database: same platform and private network as the application hosting; fully managed: no operations work for a team without DevOps.

alternatives.why_not: Azure SQL Database scores higher on reuse of existing systems and cloud preference (fit 7.7 vs 9.0).

warnings.message: ISO 27001/SOC 2 certify your controls, not the stack: providers with attestations were chosen so you inherit their controls, but you still need policies, access reviews and audits.
CERT-In Directions (2022): keep ICT system logs for 180 days within Indian jurisdiction.
'Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)': Renamed only; fully supported. Treated as Microsoft Entra ID (same service).
'Microsoft 365': reused for notifications/approvals through Microsoft Graph (Outlook/Teams).
'Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD)': reused as the identity provider (OIDC/SAML SSO, group-based roles).

'On-prem SQL Server 2019': kept as the system of record for existing data and integrated via an App Service Hybrid Connection; new data lives in SQL Server (Azure SQL) (migrate with Azure DMS/AWS DMS when ready).

'On-prem SQL Server 2019' (SQL Server 2019) is out of mainstream support; security fixes only until 2030-01-08. Mainstream support ended 28 Feb 2025; security updates only. Plan an upgrade to SQL Server 2022/2025 or Azure SQL.
